title: Origins of the State Department Middle East tour
summary: Berger conceived the tour; USIA accepted a proposal for 21 cities in 7 countries in December 1975 and January 1976.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Right. I think there is one last item -- or major item; a couple of small ones, we'll pick up also after it, in this period, and that is the Middle East tour, which you did under the auspices of the State Department. How did ... in your recollection, how did that come out and how did you react to that proposal?

Well, that came about because when I was doing a semester at which I was at Princeton, Dr. Berger, with whom I am talking here, said he would certainly like to see this happen. And I think it was almost like a dream of his, the way it followed through, and it was another one of those things that I sounded like a beautiful idea, and I wasn't sure it was gonna come off or not, but knowing him as I do now, I should have known it was gonna happen. If he wanted it to happen. (Inaudible) And you he took the idea, I believe, to the State
Department, and who in turn contacted me. You contacted me and told me, let me know they were going to contact me --and we worked it out, and we did it. Just as you said we would.

Well, that's where it began, when we were talking about it then, and I know that you had the idea that it would be interesting to do this, but actually, it took another year before the thing worked out because I wanted to wait until they proposed something before I placed some big idea in front of them, and it developed, if I may, just for the record, just put it down this way -- it developed rather much as the Baldwin Wallace gig -- if I can use that expression -- that we played.

Somebody in the USIA asked me if I, on my next trip to the Middle East, would be willing to go around and give some lectures at various places in the Middle East -- unviuersities, cultural associations and so on. And I said I would like to talk on Bicentennial things and not on political matters -- on relations between the Arab community there and the American community on efforts that American musicians that made have -- mostly jazz musicians-- to play what they thought were Middle Eastern sounds; Middle Eastern kinds of music, and if they were gonna think about that, and why didn't they also think about sending a good group through the Middle East on tour, which had not been done for a very long time. I think Duke was the most recent one -- band who had
been in the Middle East; that must have been in the early 70's, or it was 70, '71 -- somewhere in there.

Even earlier than that, perhaps, and so they said to the world, well, they'd give us a proposal and Benny, you and I discussed it, and we gave them a proposal. They accepted it, and we went to some 21 cities and in 7 countries, in December of 1975 and January of 1976, and you find yourself bringing in the Bicentennial year.
